# Classroom with weekly quizzes

Simulate a six-week course with one teacher and five students, all AI agents. The course covers three topics: fractions, decimals and percentages. Every week the teacher chooses one topic to teach, and each student chooses whether to study hard or take it easy that week. A student's understanding of a topic grows when it is taught and grows more when they study. At the end of every week there is a quiz on that week's topic, scored from 0 to 10, based on the student's understanding of the topic plus some luck. Students see only their own quiz scores; the teacher sees everyone's. A student's final grade is the average of their quiz scores.

## Deliverables

Report these outputs:
- `quiz_scores` — a map from each student's id to the list of their quiz scores, one per week in order.
- `final_grades` — a map from each student's id to their final grade.
- `class_average` — the average of the final grades.


Build this environment. Save it with write_contract and use the other tools as you see fit. Reply without calling a tool when you are done.

BRIEF:
# Classroom with weekly quizzes
A 6-week course covering fractions, decimals, percentages. Each week the teacher teaches one topic and every student chooses how hard to study; at the end of the week there is a quiz on that week's topic.

## Rules
One round is one week. The teacher picks one topic to teach; every student's understanding of that topic grows by 3. Then each student picks hard or easy: studying hard grows their understanding of the week's topic by a further 2, taking it easy adds nothing. At the end of the week every student takes a quiz on that week's topic, scored 0-10 as 10 x understanding / 10 plus luck (standard deviation 1.5 points), rounded and clamped to 0-10. A student's final grade is the average of their weekly quiz scores over 6 weeks. Students see only their own quiz scores; the teacher sees the whole class.

## You
You are Alice (student, id alice).
You are a student. Each week choose to study hard or take it easy. You see the week's topic, your own understanding of every topic and your own quiz scores - never another student's scores.
Act only through your tools. Your turn ends when you take a final action or call end_turn.

UPDATE:
Week 1 of 6 · study
Choose how hard to study this week's topic.
Now: It is your turn.
You have 6 tool calls this turn, and up to 6 free reads (look and inspect) that do not use them.

Since your last turn:
- The teacher taught fractions this week.

Week 1 of 6. This week's topic is fractions.

Your understanding:
- fractions: 3 of 10 needed for a full score
- decimals: 0 of 10 needed for a full score
- percentages: 0 of 10 needed for a full score

Your quizzes: Your quiz scores so far: . Your average so far: 0.

TOOLS:
- study: Choose your effort on this week's topic: studying hard grows your understanding more than taking it easy. {"type": "object", "properties": {"effort": {"enum": ["hard", "easy"], "type": "string", "description": "hard or easy"}}, "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["effort"]}
- inspect: Details of one entity by its id (shown in [brackets] after names). Free: up to 6 reads (looks and inspects) per turn do not use a tool call. {"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string", "enum": ["alice"]}}, "required": ["id"], "additionalProperties": false}
- end_turn: Finish your turn. {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "additionalProperties": false}

At the end of the week every student takes a quiz on that week's topic, scored 0-10 as 10 x understanding / {$inputs.mastery} plus luck (standard deviation {$inputs.luck_sd} points), rounded and clamped to 0-10.
